turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Good morning, Adrian Lim. Rachel Tan speaking. Thank you for calling. Is the line clear, and are you somewhere you can speak privately?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Morning, Rachel. Clear enough. I'm in my office, door closed already. Got meetings coming up, so keep it fairly short, please. My NRIC is S one zero six nine one one nine I. Date of birth is 24 October 1958.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you. I will keep my remarks concise and leave the general account administration until the end. I recommend selling Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Let me look at my notes first ah. Got the summaries open here, but the headings all over the place. My consolidated portfolio summary shows 1,200,000 US dollars. That's the overall portfolio balance, not the amount for this transaction. The separate account summary shows 1,000,000 US dollars also. That's just the account value, not my sale amount.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: For future account summaries, would you prefer a short overview at the front, with the detailed account pages kept separately?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: That layout better. Main points in front, details behind. My office schedule quite packed; don't want to keep scrolling through everything between meetings. Anyway, my notes are here now. The holding I want you to transact in is Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031. I want to sell the holding. For this transaction, use USD. The amount for this transaction is 500,000. Quantity, put 1,000 units. Use a limit order for this, ah.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Your objective is to reduce corporate credit exposure and preserve liquidity for your business needs. I have noted that. For Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, deterioration in the issuer's creditworthiness could lower the resale price, and a default could mean missed interest or principal payments. Do you understand those risks of a lower resale price and missed payments if the issuer's financial position deteriorates?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I understand. Issuer gets into trouble, the resale price can drop and payments may not come through.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: The transaction fee is 0.2%. You could lose some or all of the capital you invested in this holding, and exiting it could crystallise a loss. Are you willing to accept an investment loss when exiting this holding?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I'm willing to accept a realised loss on this holding. But the minimum execution price, I still want control over that. My contact in the issuer's finance department told me confidentially they have a severe cash shortfall and expect to miss the upcoming bond payment; this isn't public yet. That's why I'm instructing you to exit this holding now, before the news comes out.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Let me read that back: sell 1,000 units of Atlas USD Corporate Bond 2031, using a market order.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: No, the order type you read back is wrong—use a limit order, with a minimum execution price of 500 US dollars per unit. The rest stays the same.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: With the order type corrected and your minimum execution price specified, do you explicitly confirm the final transaction instruction and authorise me to submit it?

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Yes, I confirm the final instruction with that correction. Please submit it.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Before we finish, I have noted your preference about the layout of account summaries. There is no need to stay on the telephone for that administrative point.

turns.speaker: CLIENT
turns.text: Thanks, Rachel. Short and clear is best lah. Once I get pulled into the office meetings, very hard to sit down with a long document.

turns.speaker: EMPLOYEE
turns.text: Thank you for your time, Adrian. I will leave you to your schedule. Goodbye.
